key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with optimized DDFW settings substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, and a deep learning model can predict tensile performance with moderate accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical route to stronger lightweight aluminum joints for aerospace and automotive structures by pairing joint-geometry design with data-driven process optimization.
method: L18 orthogonal array experiments on AA2024-T351 DDFW
Compared friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying surface geometry, and friction time
Trained deep learning predictors, including an ensemble residual network, to estimate ultimate tensile strength
evidence_signal: The best setting (30 MPa friction pressure, 70 MPa forging pressure, 2200 rpm, drilled-to-bossed geometry, 4 min) achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, while the best model reached about R² = 0.81.
watch_item: The predictive model accuracy is only moderate, so broader validation on more welding conditions and independent test data would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
